guide.summary: Draft schematic assembly guide for a rectangular metal bedside table with two solid panels, four angle-section legs and sixteen screws. Start screws loosely, then align the upright table and finish tightening.
reviewNotes: Saved demonstration draft. The final visual review was not completed; compare each operation with the original manual.

Draft only: shapes, joint locations and dimensions are approximate. Overall proportions follow the drawings and the corroborating 37:28:45 label proportions, uniformly scaled to approximately 2 units high.

Working poses and leg introductions were corrected against the six main source drawings. Signed camera direction and page-up axes preserve the illustrated handedness; the fixed viewer rotates the object to match them.
Front is not marked in the manual. The left/back/right working labels use a consistent inferred convention.
Both panels have continuous metal sheet faces and four integral folded rims. Each leg consists of two joined perpendicular flanges forming an open L section.
The foot-end feature is visible, but whether it is formed or factory fitted is unresolved; no separate cap inventory is established.
The paired screw codes identify one illustrated type with sixteen instances, not two sets of sixteen. No loose washers or nuts are depicted.

Screw heads have outward-opening recessed drive cavities, represented schematically with rings. The permitted primitives approximate, rather than reproduce, the six-sided socket profile and screw threads.
Muted grey represents metal. Exact finish, sheet thickness, section widths and tool dimensions are not established by the diagrams.
Use two people and a soft protective work surface as advised on page 5. Do not sit on the table. The maximum total product load is 10 kg (22 lb), not a separate allowance for each panel.
Animated turns are decorative, not torque instructions. Final tightening is a condensed sixteen-joint overview; the source does not specify a corner-by-corner order.

steps.title: Attach the first leg to the lower shelf
steps.instruction: Support the lower shelf on an edge, with the first leg extending horizontally. Fit the leg's L-section around the illustrated shelf corner. Insert two screws, one through each perpendicular leg flange into the corresponding folded shelf rim, and engage them with the hex key without fully tightening. Reposition the subassembly afterward using the lower-right turning diagram.

At each of the two exposed tabletop corners, insert one screw through each perpendicular leg flange into the corresponding folded tabletop rim, four screws total. Leave them partly tightened. Roll the assembly onto the opposite side as indicated by the lower-right arrow.

components.name: Rectangular tabletop panel
components.description: One broad, continuous rectangular sheet panel with shallow folded perimeter rims. Its solid upper face is visible on pages 1 and 12; the separate panel is introduced in the lower-right drawing on page 9. Two perpendicular rim faces at each corner receive screws through the enclosing leg flanges. The folded rims are not separately installed rails. Preserve unequal plan dimensions and a thickness small relative to both.

components.name: Rectangular lower shelf panel
components.description: One broad, continuous rectangular sheet panel with shallow folded perimeter rims, established in step 1. Its solid surface is confirmed by the cover and final perspective. It has approximately the tabletop's footprint and sits above the legs' midpoint, leaving longer leg portions below it than above. The unshaded underside and outlined perimeter in assembly views do not establish an open frame or separate rails.

components.name: Full-height L-section corner leg
components.description: Four individual long members, introduced as one in step 1, one in step 2, and two in step 3. Each consists of two perpendicular thin flange faces sharing a continuous longitudinal bend: an open L/angle section, not two supports or a closed square tube. Each leg wraps one corner of both panels and receives four screws, one through each flange at each panel level. The first leg on page 7 visibly has a finished foot-end outline, and page 8 enlarges that feature on a leg. Whether the end feature is formed or a separately manufactured fitted cap is not established.

components.name: Short flanged hex-socket screw
components.description: Short threaded screw with a broad, low round flange head and internal hex socket. Page 6 depicts one screw type with a total quantity of sixteen and prints both codes beside it; it does not explain code applicability or assign sixteen to each code. Each screw joins one leg flange to one folded panel rim. No separate loose washers or nuts are illustrated.

components.name: L-shaped hex key
components.description: One slim L-shaped key with unequal perpendicular arms and hexagonal working ends. Page 6 gives its code and quantity; the assembly details show it engaging the screws' internal hex sockets. It is a removable assembly tool, not a permanent table component.

referenceViews.description: Upright table with two continuous rectangular surfaces and four corner legs. Four distinct foot ends are visible: left, foreground, right, and the partly occluded rear foot near the image center. The central-looking member traces to the rear panel corner; it is not an additional center support. The foreground leg's two visible faces belong to one L-section member. Overall height exceeds either horizontal dimension.

The lower-right handling thumbnail shows the completed assembly being turned onto its four feet after the last four screws are inserted. Both panels and all four legs are existing components. The thumbnail and turning arrow introduce no additional parts.

The main upright perspective confirms two solid panels and four distinct corner legs, including the rear leg partly hidden by both panels. The magnified detail shows the hex key tightening an existing screw through a leg flange into the tabletop rim.

The bottom alignment inset contrasts a straight, square assembly with a crossed-out racked assembly. The panels are viewed edge-on. Their horizontal outlines are not additional rails, and the overlapping front/rear projections do not reduce the four-leg inventory.

reviewNotes: Reviewed the supplied evidence for all twelve pages. Pages 2–4 contain warnings; page 5 contains generic assembly advice rather than a product-specific parts inventory. The physical reconstruction relies on the cover, page 6 hardware illustrations, every numbered main drawing and detail, and the completed views.

The four-leg quantity survives the distinct-instance check: step 1 introduces one, step 2 introduces one, and step 3 introduces two. Cover and final views show four corresponding foot ends. The partly occluded member near the image center is the rear corner leg, and the two faces of an L-section leg are not separate supports. No fifth support or separately installed rail is established.

Permanent primary-piece introductions reconcile to one lower shelf established in step 1, four legs introduced across steps 1–3, and one tabletop introduced in the page 9 insertion thumbnail. Steps 4–6 introduce no further primary pieces. Both broad solid surfaces must remain represented despite their unshaded, frame-like underside drawings.

Fasteners reconcile exactly: four legs × two panels × two perpendicular flange-to-rim screws = sixteen screws. New insertions are 2 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 4; step 6 only tightens those same sixteen. Projected vertical arrows do not establish holes through either broad panel surface.

The visible page 6 inventory supports one key coded 100006 and sixteen screws bearing the paired codes 10118490 and 10118469. It does not explain the relationship between the screw codes. Other codes in the parsed text cannot be matched to additional visible inventory items and do not support extra hardware quantities.

The label's nominal 37 × 28 × 45 cm dimensions are consistent with a non-square rectangular footprint and a height exceeding either horizontal dimension. Preserve approximate overall proportions of 37:28:45, but do not treat these as exact individual-panel dimensions. The manual does not provide panel measurements, section widths, sheet thicknesses, screw dimensions, or tool size. Black finish is metadata context, not a parts-list fact.

The foot-end feature is positively visible on the leg being attached in step 1 and in the page 8 enlargement. Its manufacturing method and possible separate cap identity remain unresolved; no additional supplied-cap inventory or factory-attachment process is established. Similarly, the panels' matching construction does not establish interchangeability.

Each main drawing was checked separately: steps 1–5 have horizontal leg axes and panels on edge, not supports pointing upward from an inverted tabletop. The turns distinguish successive handling poses; steps 3–4 share a pose and step 5 follows a roll to the opposite side. The retained left/back/right labels are a consistent inferred convention because no front is marked. Step 6 is unambiguously upright. This remains a schematic document-based draft, not proof of physical correctness.
